blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

Rubber

T. and W. Musgrove discuss the origins and early uses of rubber

The plants that produce rubber are spread right across the globe, and grow in many different habitats. One might think it likely, therefore, that humankind has known about rubber for thousands of years. Yet, unlike other crops of economic importance, rubber led a relatively anonymous life until the last 150 years or so. The Indians of South America appear to be the first people to have understood the properties of rubber, and the Aztecs of what is now Mexico were the first to be recorded using the substance; a wall painting dating back to the sixth century depicts a scene of a tribute offering of crude rubber. With the arrival of Columbus in the Americas and the resulting Spanish influx, further evidence starts to appear concerning the Native American use of rubber. Antonio de Herrera y Tordesillas describes a ritual game played with a rubber ball at the court of the Aztec Emperor Montezuma II, and the Mayan and Toltec people are known to have taken part in similar activities. Rubber was also used to make raincoats, shoes, jars, torches and musical instruments, all of which must have been made from the indigenous Castilla elastica, as the Para rubber plant now favoured for rubber cultivation does not grow in the Mexican region.

The first description of latex (liquid rubber) extraction was made by Juan de Torquemada, who noted that if a receptacle was not at hand the Native Americans would place the latex on their bodies to allow it to solidify. However, no real interest in rubber was shown by any European until Charles de la Condamine, a French mathematician, published an account of his journey to South America in 1735. The journey was undertaken on behalf of the Paris Academy of Sciences to measure an arc of the meridian line on the equator, but the journey home was to turn out to be more significant than the true purpose of the trip. Condamine explored Brazil and Peru and discovered how the local people used one single piece of coagulated latex to make boots. The boots were impervious to water and, when smoked, looked like real leather. In 1747 the first description of the rubber tree and latex tapping was made by a military engineer and amateur botanist, François Fresneau, who was posted to French Guiana. The publications of Condamine and Fresneau created considerable excitement among French scientists, and an attempt was made to discover a solvent that could turn the crude rubber into a substance for commercial exploitation.

In 1818 a British medical student named James Syme first used rubber to make waterproof cloth. Another early use of the substance was as an eraser of pencil marks, hence the name 'rubber'. This was complemented by balloons, rubber bands, braces, boots for the army and other ideas that met with varying degrees of success. In 1820 Thomas Hancock, an English manufacturer of rubber goods such as driving belts, industrial rollers and rubber hoses, invented a machine he called the ‘masticator', which chewed up waste strips for re-use. It was discovered that the masticated rubber was more malleable, while maintaining much of its elasticity. In Scotland at the same time, Charles Mackintosh had discovered a way of using rubber as waterproofing material, by a process he patented in 1823. Hancock and Mackintosh joined forces in 1834, and three years later Hancock invented a machine for spreading rubber onto material.

Despite their beneficial qualities, such as waterproofing, rubber goods were still not particularly popular as they had some major flaws, including the fact that they dissolved malodorously. They also became pliant when warm and rigid when cold. Then in 1839 the American Charles Goodyear discovered that it was possible to stabilise rubber by mixing it with sulphur while exposing it to heat — a process he called vulcanisation — and the full versatility of this extraordinary substance became apparent.

Rubber goods could now be manufactured which had all the beneficial qualities of the material, such as durability, elasticity and variability, but which were not sticky, soluble or governed by the vagaries of the weather. The economic potential of rubber was now clearly evident. It played an important role in the Industrial Revolution, being employed in the steam engines found in factories, mills, mines and railways. It made a triumphant entrance as a new and innovative material at the Great Exhibition of 1851, where shoes, airbeds, furniture and clothing made out of newly improved rubber were proudly displayed.

One of the most important rubber inventions was made in 1888, when an Irishman called John Boyd Dunlop produced the first pneumatic tyre. Solid rubber tyres had been used for the previous 18 years, but Dunlop's new design, which he updated in 1890, immediately became popular. In 1895 Dunlop's tyres were first used in motor cars, and with the mass production of cars just over the horizon the rubber industry had never looked healthier. The import levels of rubber over the nineteenth century bear witness to its irrepressible rise. In 1830 Britain had imported just 211 kg of crude rubber. This had risen to 10,000 kg in 1857, and by 1874 levels were just under six times as much again.

Questions 1–6

Do the following statements agree with the information in Reading Passage 1?

In boxes 1–6 on your answer sheet, write:

  • TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
  • FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
  • NOT GIVEN if there is no information about this

1. Rubber plants grow only in certain regions of the world.

2. Rubber was extracted in Mexico as early as the sixth century.

3. Rubber from the Castilla elastica plant is of poorer quality than that from the Para plant.

4. A French mathematician inspired real interest in rubber amongst Europeans.

5. The process of vulcanisation was discovered by accident.

6. Imports of crude rubber into Britain fell during the nineteenth century.

Questions 7–13

Complete the summary below.

Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.

The Commercial Development of Rubber

Early European travellers gave accounts of various rubber objects in use in Central and South America, and these accounts created interest in the commercial exploitation of rubber. In 1818, 7 was produced using rubber, and in 1820 a machine was invented for recycling 8 of rubber. Over the next few years, other attempts were made to improve rubber, but some problems remained. For example, rubber products smelt bad when they were dissolved, and could turn either soft or 9 depending on the temperature. However, in 1839 a new process to 10 the substance greatly increased its potential. For example, rubber was used in the creation of the 11 industry during the Industrial Revolution. Then in 1888 the 12 was developed, and a few years later the 13 of the motor car began.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 橡胶树广泛分布于全球不同栖息地，但与其他经济作物不同，橡胶在近 150 年才被广泛关注。南美洲印第安人最早了解橡胶特性，墨西哥阿兹特克人是有记载的最早使用者 ——6 世纪的壁画描绘了进贡生橡胶的场景。哥伦布抵达美洲后，欧洲人逐渐了解美洲原住民对橡胶的使用：安东尼奥・德・埃雷拉・托德西利亚斯（Antonio de Herrera y Tordesillas）记载了阿兹特克皇帝蒙特祖马二世宫廷中用橡胶球进行的仪式游戏，玛雅人和托尔特克人也有类似活动。当时的橡胶制品（雨衣、鞋子、罐子等）均来自当地的 Castilla elastica 树，因如今用于橡胶种植的 Para 橡胶树并不生长在墨西哥地区。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 胡安・德・托尔克马达（Juan de Torquemada）首次描述了乳胶（液态橡胶）的提取方式 —— 美洲原住民在没有容器时，会将乳胶涂在身上使其凝固。但欧洲人对橡胶真正产生兴趣，始于法国数学家夏尔・德・拉孔达明（Charles de la Condamine）1735 年发表的南美旅行报告。他最初受巴黎科学院委托测量赤道子午线弧度，但返程中的发现更具意义：他在巴西和秘鲁发现当地人用一块凝固乳胶制作防水靴（烟熏后类似真皮）。1747 年，派驻法属圭亚那的军事工程师兼业余植物学家弗朗索瓦・弗雷斯诺（François Fresneau）首次描述了橡胶树和乳胶采集方法。拉孔达明和弗雷斯诺的著作引发法国科学家的浓厚兴趣，他们开始尝试寻找能将生橡胶转化为商业可用材料的溶剂。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 1818 年，英国医学生詹姆斯・赛姆（James Syme）首次用橡胶制作防水布；橡胶早期另一用途是擦除铅笔痕迹，“rubber”（橡皮擦）一词也由此而来。此后，气球、橡皮筋、背带、军靴等橡胶制品陆续出现，但成功率各异。1820 年，英国橡胶制品制造商托马斯・汉考克（Thomas Hancock）发明 “咀嚼机（masticator）”，可将橡胶废料条重新加工利用，且加工后的橡胶更易塑形，同时保留大部分弹性。同期在苏格兰，查尔斯・麦金托什（Charles Mackintosh）发现橡胶防水用法，并于 1823 年获得专利。1834 年，汉考克与麦金托什合作，三年后汉考克发明橡胶涂覆机，可将橡胶涂在材料上。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 尽管橡胶具有防水等优点，但橡胶制品存在重大缺陷：溶解时气味难闻，且遇热变软、遇冷变硬。1839 年，美国人查尔斯・古德伊尔（Charles Goodyear）发现 “硫化（vulcanisation）” 工艺 —— 将橡胶与硫磺混合并加热，可使橡胶性质稳定，橡胶的全面实用性由此显现。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 硫化后的橡胶制品兼具耐用性、弹性和可塑性，且不再发黏、可溶解或受天气影响，橡胶的经济潜力彻底释放。橡胶在工业革命中发挥重要作用，被用于工厂、磨坊、矿山和铁路的蒸汽机；1851 年万国博览会上，改良橡胶制成的鞋子、气垫床、家具和服装亮相，橡胶作为创新材料崭露头角。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 1888 年，爱尔兰人约翰・博伊德・邓洛普（John Boyd Dunlop）发明首个充气轮胎 —— 此前 18 年一直使用实心橡胶轮胎，他 1890 年改进的设计迅速流行。1895 年，邓洛普轮胎首次用于汽车，随着汽车量产时代即将到来，橡胶行业迎来繁荣。19 世纪英国橡胶进口量印证了其快速发展：1830 年仅进口 211 公斤生橡胶，1857 年增至 10000 公斤，1874 年接近 1857 年的 6 倍。

items.text:
题目：Rubber plants grow only in certain regions of the world.
题目翻译：橡胶树只生长在世界上某些特定地区。
答案：FALSE
解析：开头明确写橡胶树分布在全球不同栖息地，不是“只在少数地区生长”。

题目：Rubber was extracted in Mexico as early as the sixth century.
题目翻译：早在 6 世纪，墨西哥就已开始提取橡胶。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：文章提到 6 世纪壁画记录了生橡胶进贡和使用，但没有直接说明“提取工艺”已在当时墨西哥实施到题干所述程度。

题目：Rubber from the Castilla elastica plant is of poorer quality than that from the Para plant.
题目翻译：Castilla elastica 树产出的橡胶质量低于 Para 橡胶树。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：文中仅说明中美洲制品来自 Castilla elastica，且 Para 树不生长于墨西哥，没有质量优劣比较信息。

题目：A French mathematician inspired real interest in rubber amongst Europeans.
题目翻译：一位法国数学家激发了欧洲人对橡胶的真正兴趣。
答案：TRUE
解析：拉孔达明 1735 年发表南美见闻后，法国科学界开始系统研究橡胶，题干与原文一致。

题目：The process of vulcanisation was discovered by accident.
题目翻译：硫化工艺是偶然发现的。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：文章只写古德伊尔在 1839 年发现硫化工艺，没有交代发现过程是否“偶然”。

题目：Imports of crude rubber into Britain fell during the nineteenth century.
题目翻译：19 世纪英国进口生橡胶数量下降。
答案：FALSE
解析：文末给出数据是持续增长：1830 年 211 公斤，1857 年 10000 公斤，1874 年接近其 6 倍。

questionExplanations.text:
题目 1：橡胶树是否只在少数地区生长。答案：FALSE。解析：原文说分布广泛。
题目 2：6 世纪墨西哥是否已明确提取橡胶。答案：NOT GIVEN。解析：只提到使用与进贡记录。
题目 3：Castilla 与 Para 橡胶质量比较。答案：NOT GIVEN。解析：文中未做质量对比。
题目 4：法国数学家是否推动欧洲兴趣。答案：TRUE。解析：拉孔达明报告后研究热度上升。
题目 5：硫化是否偶然发现。答案：NOT GIVEN。解析：未说明发现方式。
题目 6：19 世纪英国橡胶进口是否下降。答案：FALSE。解析：数据体现显著上升。

items.text:
题目：In 1818, ____ was produced using rubber.
题目翻译：1818 年，利用橡胶制成了 ____。
答案：waterproof cloth
解析：原文写 James Syme 在 1818 年首次用橡胶制作 waterproof cloth。

题目：In 1820 a machine was invented for recycling ____ of rubber.
题目翻译：1820 年发明了一台机器，用于回收橡胶 ____。
答案：waste strips
解析：汉考克的 masticator 用于重新处理橡胶废条，答案对应 waste strips。

题目：Rubber could turn either soft or ____ depending on the temperature.
题目翻译：橡胶会随温度变化而变软或变得 ____。
答案：rigid
解析：文中指出橡胶遇热变软、遇冷变硬，空格应为 rigid。

题目：In 1839 a new process to ____ the substance greatly increased its potential.
题目翻译：1839 年，一种用于 ____ 这种材料的新工艺大幅提升了其潜力。
答案：stabilise
解析：硫化工艺核心就是让橡胶性质稳定，文意对应 stabilise。

题目：Rubber was used in the creation of the ____ industry during the Industrial Revolution.
题目翻译：工业革命期间，橡胶被用于 ____ 产业/系统的构建。
答案：steam engines
解析：文章明确写橡胶被用于工厂、矿山和铁路的 steam engines。

题目：Then in 1888 the ____ was developed.
题目翻译：随后在 1888 年，____ 被开发出来。
答案：pneumatic tyre
解析：文中说 Dunlop 于 1888 年发明首个充气轮胎，即 pneumatic tyre。

题目：A few years later the ____ of the motor car began.
题目翻译：几年后，汽车的 ____ 开始了。
答案：mass production
解析：文章结尾指出汽车量产时代到来，对应 mass production。

questionExplanations.text:
题目 7：1818 年橡胶制成何物。答案：waterproof cloth。解析：直接对应 James Syme 叙述。
题目 8：1820 年机器回收何种橡胶材料。答案：waste strips。解析：masticator 用于废条再利用。
题目 9：橡胶温度变化后的另一状态。答案：rigid。解析：冷时变硬。
题目 10：新工艺的作用。答案：stabilise。解析：硫化让性质稳定。
题目 11：工业革命中关联行业。答案：steam engines。解析：蒸汽机应用场景明确。
题目 12：1888 年开发成果。答案：pneumatic tyre。解析：邓禄普发明充气轮胎。
题目 13：随后开始的汽车阶段。答案：mass production。解析：文末指向汽车量产。
